summary: Milestone 2026.05.259 produced 0 experiment commits in the timing window — the thirty-fourth consecutive empty-timing-window retro — due to the timing script's look-back not being anchored to the conductor-state.json activation timestamp. Both RTX 3090 GPUs were fully idle (0% utilization, 41C/49C) throughout; gpu_idle_on_compute_bound_tasks is null because no compute-bound tasks appear in the timing scope. Twelve experiments (exp2727–exp2737 plus the capstone) were completed outside the timing window and are documented in the changelog but cannot be counted here.
bottlenecks_identified: Timing-script look-back window is not anchored to conductor-state.json activated_at timestamp — root cause of 34 consecutive empty-timing-window retros; all real experiment work falls outside the measurement window.
No post-activation dispatch verification gate: the conductor can complete activation and write the retro without confirming that at least one non-retro experiment was dispatched in the same session.

Persistent infrastructure debt: the look-back fix has been the top leverage action for 34 consecutive milestones without being implemented, indicating no closed feedback loop between retro recommendations and roadmap planning.
improvements_suggested: Anchor the timing data extraction script to conductor-state.json activated_at rather than a fixed look-back window; this would immediately resolve the empty-timing-window problem.
Wire a zero-artifact alarm that fires 60 minutes after milestone activation if no non-retro experiment commit has landed; alert the operator before the retro is written.
Require the conductor to dispatch the first non-retro experiment in the same session as milestone activation, so at least one experiment always falls within the timing window.

Add an infrastructure-slot enforcement check: if the same improvement has appeared in improvements_suggested for 5+ consecutive milestones without a corresponding YAML task, auto-elevate it to MANDATORY-NEXT-MILESTONE PRIORITIES in ops/known-issues.md.
top_3_highest_leverage_actions: Fix scripts/session-metrics.py (or equivalent timing extractor) to use conductor-state.json activated_at as the look-back anchor — eliminates the empty-timing-window problem for all future milestones in a single one-time fix.
Wire a post-activation zero-artifact alarm at T+60min — prevents the retro from being the first artifact written after activation by surfacing the gap to the operator in real time.

Add a roadmap-level infrastructure task for the timing fix in .260 with a doomed-rerun block if it has appeared in improvements_suggested for 5+ prior milestones — closes the feedback loop between retro output and planner input.
meta_reflection: For the thirty-fourth consecutive milestone, the retro's most actionable finding is the same: fix the timing-script look-back. The fact that this recommendation has not propagated into a concrete roadmap task indicates a structural gap in the feedback loop between retro output and planner input — the retro writes into ops/changelog.md but no mechanism reads retro improvements_suggested when drafting research-roadmap-next.yaml. Closing that loop — even by a simple grep of the retro's top_3_highest_leverage_actions into the known-issues.md MANDATORY-NEXT-MILESTONE PRIORITIES section — would have higher expected value than any single experiment proposed for .260.
